name: Advantage and Disadvantage
description: When you have advantage on a roll, roll a second d20 and use the higher of the two. With disadvantage, use the lower. If circumstances grant both advantage and disadvantage, they cancel and you roll a single d20. Advantage and disadvantage don't stack.

name: Cover
description: Half cover grants +2 to AC and Dexterity saving throws. Three-quarters cover grants +5. A target with total cover can't be targeted directly by an attack or spell.

name: Resting
description: A short rest is a period of at least 1 hour during which a creature can spend Hit Dice to regain hit points. A long rest is at least 8 hours; a creature regains all lost hit points and recovers spent Hit Dice up to half its total.

name: Death Saving Throws
description: When you start your turn at 0 hit points, roll a d20. 10 or higher is a success; 9 or lower is a failure. Three successes stabilize you; three failures mean death. A natural 20 restores 1 hit point; a natural 1 counts as two failures. Taking damage at 0 HP is one failure (a critical hit is two).

name: Exhaustion
description: Exhaustion is measured in six levels: 1 disadvantage on ability checks; 2 speed halved; 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws; 4 hit point maximum halved; 5 speed reduced to 0; 6 death. A long rest reduces exhaustion by one level (with food and drink).
